Truk_response_gate.physical_capability: PASS; five-deck system can now mount a meaningful one-cycle battle strike.
Truk_response_gate.command_release: HOLD; Truk defense alone is not a release condition.
Truk_response_gate.operational_slack: IMPROVING but carrier-air cadre remains the strategic asset being rebuilt.
Truk_response_gate.motive_payoff: FAIL; no transports, no persistent landing geometry, and the US force is a short-duration raid package.
Truk_response_gate.information_quality: HIGH warning / LOCAL weapon quality only; no stable long-range track on withdrawal.
Truk_response_gate.opportunity_cost: VERY HIGH; sacrificing five-deck cohesion for Truk would exchange the principal Japanese 1944 recovery asset for a target that can disengage at will.

carrier_decision: NO-GO FOR MOBILE-FLEET INTERCEPT. Hold southern reaction/training system, raise readiness, use local air/submarines/recon to harass and learn from the raid.

Tatsumaki_review.historical_concept: April training for a Majuro attack using several submarines carrying torpedo-armed amphibious vehicles.
reasons: low probability of undetected delivery and successful overland/water attack
ties several useful submarines to a gimmick mission during a period when carrier-warning pickets and reconnaissance are strategically valuable
poor extraction/recovery logic and weak expected damage against a dispersed US anchorage
branch information culture values repeatable cueing/ISR utility over one-shot novelty absent an exceptional target
Tatsumaki_review.resource_reallocation: Keep candidate submarines in training/readiness and redirect deployable boats toward Central-Pacific warning, reconnaissance and anti-logistics patrols rather than fixing them to the Majuro special attack.
